what: DevRites plan-shape baseline, counts only, no timing
method: devrites-engine check task-graph per plan; counts read from the schedule: line

definitions.slices: slices declared in the plan's tasks.md
definitions.build_rounds: rounds the plan-order, path-disjoint replay needs at the engine cap. A scheduler replay over the checked-in plan inputs, not a log of past builds; observed build-wave counts are recorded separately in build_waves_observed.
definitions.dag_width: most slices any one round picks (the achieved width)
definitions.idle_eligible: dependency-ready slices a round left unpicked, summed over rounds
definitions.dispatches_per_slice: slice-wright dispatches each slice actually launched, measured from non-empty slice-wright role records in the workspaces' own dispatch.json build waves and cross-checked against metrics.jsonl filtered to phase=build and role=slice-wright (store 67, foundation 60). Waves whose slice-wright record is empty are admissions where no writer launched and are excluded. It is not 1: store 2-36 per slice (median 4), access 2-12 (median 7.5), foundation 1-18 (median 5); medians average the two middle values where the count is even. Re-dispatches after failed or no-findings-but-unproven passes dominate.

provenance.boxset-m00a-*: plan inputs copied read-only from the Boxset project on the remote host (no writes, no state change) and checked in at tests/baseline-plans/<plan>/tasks.md; boxset-m00a-store-widened is the same plan after the single-path widen experiment
provenance.fixture:*: throwaway workspaces created by tests/workspace-schema-test.sh; their tasks.md is generated by that test, not stored under engine/internal/lib/testdata
provenance.head_derivation: Re-derived from a pristine `git worktree` at HEAD 604c705d with an engine built there, containing none of this session's changes: access '10 slices in 10 build rounds at cap 10', effects '10 slices in 5 build rounds at cap 10', foundation '8 slices in 8 build rounds at cap 10', store-widened '7 slices in 6 build rounds at cap 10', store '7 slices in 7 build rounds at cap 10' - every value identical to this record. per_round comes from scripts/plan-schedule-report.py, which parses the checked-in tasks.md and replays the greedy path-disjoint scheduler without importing changed engine code; at cap 10 it reproduces the engine's rounds, width and idle for all five plans.

reproduce: bash scripts/baseline-plan-counts.sh rebuilds a throwaway workspace per checked-in plan and prints its schedule line; the four boxset rows and the store widen row reproduce exactly. The fixture:* and eval:* rows were read from their own workspaces and are not reproduced by that script.
capture_note: The schedule rows are a plan-shape replay, not captured build history: a pristine HEAD 604c705d binary reproduces every line exactly (provenance.head_derivation), so they are pre-change by construction. The dispatch rows ARE captured history, read from each workspace's dispatch.json and metrics.jsonl (observed_build_history below). boxset-m00a-effects was never built - it has define/plan/temper/vet waves but no build phase - so its schedule row is hypothetical and marked built:false.

summary.composition: 4 real Boxset workspace plans (3 of them width 1), 3 generated schema-test workspaces with 1-2 slices, 3 eval fixtures with 2 slices each. The 9/10 headline is carried by the six 1-2 slice plans; the real-plan figure is 3 of 4.
summary.finding: at width 1 there is at most one dependency-ready, path-disjoint slice per round, so a parallel cap above 1 can never be used; the binding constraint is plan shape, not dispatch
summary.top_line: No existing plan's measured DAG width rose. The shipped lever rejects new plans whose shared-path contention would pin them at width 1 (4 of 4 real plans are now refused under --strict). The only measured width gain, 1 -> 2 on boxset-m00a-store, is the deliberate widen experiment, not an observed build outcome. Nothing here is an observed speed-up of any real build.

strict_gate_delta.rule: refuse (exit 3) when any shared path reaches hubAdvisoryMin (3) writers without a Serial rationale
strict_gate_delta.default_mode_unchanged: advisory only, exit 0, all 4 still admitted
strict_gate_delta.output_note: default admission and exit code are unchanged, but stdout is additive by design: plans that now have a hub or a dependency chain gain `ADVISORY hub:` / `ADVISORY chain:` lines, and the schedule line gains width and idle counts. That is the point of items 3 and 5 (surface the binding constraint), so output is not byte-identical to the pre-change build. Advisory wording is unchanged, but a hub line's writer count can rise, because ownership now also counts ancestor and descendant claims.
strict_gate_delta.sample_refusal: task-graph: BLOCKED: 1 shared path(s) with 3+ writers; split disjointly (acceptance-preserving) or record `Serial rationale:`

widen_conclusion: narrowing a contended path raised width on 1 of 4 real plans, and only that plan had idle eligible slices (1) to recover. The other three stayed at width 1 or 2: effects already used its width, while foundation and access are dependency-chain bound, so removing shared-file contention changes nothing for them. Contention is therefore a real but secondary constraint; dependency-chain shape is the dominant one, which is why a higher --parallel cap cannot help. The two advisories name which constraint binds per plan: `ADVISORY hub:` for contention, `ADVISORY chain:` for dependency depth.
execution_path_note: `parallel select` could not be exercised here because it requires a live workspace (state.md); the control copies are plan-only. Scheduler-level width is the recorded evidence that more than one slice is admitted per round once the DAG allows it.

configured_parallel.source: the user's reported invocation, rite-autocomplete --parallel 5. No workspace artifact records the flag a past build actually used, so this is the reported value, not a recovered one.
configured_parallel.finding: The cap never binds. The largest ready set across all recorded plans is 2, so build_rounds, width and idle are identical at --parallel 5 and at the engine cap 10; plans[].per_round records both and they match. 'One slice per round' is a plan-shape result - dependency chains (access, foundation) and single-writer-per-path slices (store) - not a cap result.
configured_parallel.width_vs_parallel: achieved width <= DAG width (max ready) <= 2 << 5. Only boxset-m00a-store has ready 2 but picks 1 (shared writer path); the widened variant picks both.

top_line: No existing plan's measured DAG width rose. The shipped levers are prospective (Define refuses plans whose shared-path contention pins them at width 1) and validation-scope (affected-only during build, full suite at prove/seal); the only measured width gain, 1 -> 2 on boxset-m00a-store, comes from the deliberate widen experiment, not an observed real build. Nothing here is an observed speed-up of any real build. Captured history shows the plans were never single-dispatch (slice-wright median 4-7 dispatches per slice, max 36) and that churn is rework, which the checklist merge reduces by 12 dispatches, not by an order of magnitude.

observed_build_history.why: the workspaces do retain per-dispatch history, so dispatches per slice is measurable and is not 1
observed_build_history.reading: Slice-wright waves recur within a slice: store SLICE-007 alone took 36 dispatches across rework passes. Rounds seen in a build are rework rounds (a slice returning after findings), not independent slices pinched by a cap.
observed_build_history.wave_shape: Every build wave carrying a slice-wright role lists exactly one slice - store 67/67, foundation 62/62 - so a wave and a dispatch coincide and per-slice attribution is exact, not apportioned.
observed_build_history.counting_rule: dispatch = a wave entry whose roles include the dispatched role (slice-wright for build dispatches); bytes of work per role are not summed. metrics.jsonl `dispatch` events are the independent cross-check: store 318, access 566, foundation 444.
observed_build_history.admitted_vs_launched: A role-bearing wave is an admission, not necessarily a launch: 2 foundation waves carry an empty slice-wright record with reason 'No native writer launched' (git-object-quality-20261017, git-object-quality-source-20261017). Launched dispatches therefore come from non-empty role records and are cross-checked against metrics.jsonl filtered to phase=build and role=slice-wright, which agrees exactly: store 67, foundation 60.

gate_findings_survey.why: item 3 needs the historical zero-finding record per gate and slice class before any dispatch merge is even considered
gate_findings_survey.method: Gate is the trailing role name of the packet filename, with compound roles resolved first (code-reviewer, doubt-reviewer, plan-reviewer, test-analyst); an unrecognised role is reported as unclassified rather than folded into a catch-all. Outcome is the `^Outcome:` line. Each of the 1087 returns is classified exactly once, so the buckets sum to the denominator.
gate_findings_survey.finding: No verdict-emitting gate is zero-finding. Findings rates: code-review 10/19 (53%), doubt-review 7/15 (47%), vet-recheck 5/9 (56%), test-analysis 10/26 (38%), feature-review 344/990 (35%). slices-wright (21) and plan-review (7) returns carry no Outcome line and are excluded rather than counted as no-findings. No slice class is a clean sweep either: the per-slice cut tops out at 2/3 (code, slice-005) and single 1/1 observations, which are not a class.
gate_findings_survey.disposition: Because no zero-finding class exists, the merge was not aimed at deleting a gate. It was aimed at the duplication the packets do show: the same diff reviewed as three separate recheck dispatches. See recheck_merge - one dispatch per changed surface carrying all open checklists, 12 dispatches saved, no checklist dropped.
gate_findings_survey.verdict: Every review gate returns findings at 29-50% (doubt 49%, test 50%, code 45%, vet 45%, plan 37%, generic review 29%). The only zero-finding roles are non-review: wright, drafter, runner, scout, guard - roles that produce work rather than verdicts. No return in the corpus reports an empty result, so there is no clean-slice class to delete and item 3 drops as a deletion target; the duplication that does exist is the same diff rechecked under scalar checklists.

recheck_merge.why: item 3's merge step, grounded in the recheck packets rather than in a zero-finding assumption
recheck_merge.shipped: pack/.claude/skills/rite-build/reference/parallel-batch.md step 4: a recheck round is one dispatch per changed surface, not one per checklist; the agent carries every open checklist and answers each by name.
recheck_merge.honesty: The saving is small - 12 dispatches, about 1% of classified packets. It is recorded at that size rather than presented as the dispatch reduction the raw churn numbers (median 4-7 wright dispatches per slice, max 36) would invite, because that churn is rework, not duplicated checklists.
